title: Lobster Roll
subtitle: creamy shellfish filling in a toasted roll
excerpt: Cooked lobster or king prawns mixed with a light mayonnaise dressing and piled into a toasted, buttered roll. This is the Connecticut-style version, served cold. Simple, quick, and impressive.
sourceNotes: The lobster roll is a New England institution, with competing cold (Connecticut) and warm (Maine) versions. It became popular at roadside seafood stands along the New England coast from the 1920s onwards.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a few hours ahead and keep refrigerated. Toast the rolls just before serving.

content.text: Keep the mayonnaise dressing light -- just enough to bind the filling. The shellfish should be the main event, not the sauce. Toast the rolls in butter until golden just before serving.

items.prepNote: use 400g cooked lobster meat -- or king prawns as a substitute
use 4 hot dog rolls or brioche rolls (shop-bought)

content.text: If using raw prawns, cook them in salted boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes until pink. Drain and cool.
Chop the cooked shellfish into rough 2cm pieces.
Mix the shellfish with the mayonnaise, lemon juice, spring onion, celery, and salt. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Toast the rolls cut-side down for 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
Pile the shellfish filling into the toasted rolls and serve straight away.

items.cause: Shellfish not drained properly or too much lemon juice
items.fix: Pat the cooked shellfish dry before mixing. Add lemon juice gradually and taste as you go.

items.cause: Filling added to untoasted roll or too far in advance
items.fix: Toast the rolls well and fill them only when ready to serve.
Remove prawns from the water the moment they curl and turn pink. They take only 2 minutes.

content.text: The lobster roll is a defining food of the New England coast. It became popular at roadside stands and clam shacks from the 1920s onwards. Connecticut claims the original cold, mayo-dressed version. Maine insists on warm lobster tossed in butter. Both are worth eating. The roll is now found across the United States and beyond.
